author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Add a syslog alert under System > Configuration > Syslog in Tenable Identity Exposure (formerly Tenable AD), pointed at the data collector over UDP or TCP, with On each deviance and On each attack. Tenable's docs call the format CEF, but each alert is an RFC 3164 header and then quoted fields. Indicator of Exposure deviances and Indicator of Attack alerts go to ThirdPartyAlert with the codename as the title, the severity, the domain and, for attacks, the source and destination hosts and addresses and the targeted user. AD change and health check messages stay in the generic schema. The parent matches the field layout after the product name, which varies by version (TenableAD, and AlsidForAD before 3.1). The header time has no year or zone, and the event time comes from the syslog header. Samples follow the IoE and IoA examples on Tenable's alert details page with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (87 of 90 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. The other 3 were the event time of the lines that keep their <PRI>: Run Test stored the ingest time, where expected.json has the reference time. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent, with the same difference. No built-in parser claimed these lines in 10 Run Tests.
